{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABa0Yqaw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhEaGYk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 16, "title": "Run a 65C816 RTL CPU with a test ROM in the browser", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL now runs a five-file CPU-style ROM/RAM bus self-test (#14), but its bus master is only a fixed state machine, **not a real CPU**. The next step toward a Super Famicom (SNES) hardware demonstration is to execute actual **65C816 machine instructions** in a browser-compiled RTL CPU core.

WebRTL must remain a general RTL development platform; the SNES is an example, not a special-purpose software emulator built into the UI.

## Expected outcome

Integrate a **real, synthesizable 65C816-compatible RTL CPU core** into a small browser-runnable example with a minimal ROM/RAM harness. The browser compiles the RTL through the existing Yosys/CXXRTL/Clang → WASM pipeline, then executes a tiny permitted machine-code test program. The program fetches instructions, performs a memory read/write, and reaches a machine-verifiable success state.

Use an appropriately licensed existing RTL core if feasible, documenting its provenance, license and any adaptations. If adapting the chosen core or writing the necessary initial CPU logic, preserve genuine CPU instruction-fetch/decode/execute behavior; do **not** simulate a hardcoded test script in JavaScript or replace the CPU with another fixed bus sequencer.

## Scope

- Select and integrate a 65C816 RTL implementation compatible with the currently supported synthesizable HDL subset. Document the core/source, license, supported instructions/modes, and modifications. Avoid introducing VHDL or an unrelated second compiler in this task.
- Connect the CPU's actual bus pins/phases to a *small* ROM/RAM harness. Adapt the existing #14 bus logic where helpful, but explicitly handle and document differences such as the CPU's **24-bit addressing**, read/write strobes, reset sequence, and timing. Do not claim that the simple #14 one-cycle protocol is already SNES-compatible.
- Provide a deterministic, inline test ROM with the correct 65C816 reset-vector mapping and a short program in a documented mode (e.g. 8-bit emulation mode). Exercise **instruction fetch, immediate arithmetic/load, a RAM store/readback, and a conditional branch or completion indication** using actual CPU instructions.
- Expose a minimal, automated-testable result (PASS/FAIL and/or sampled CPU PC/register/bus trace) via a focused example adapter. Keep the RTL CPU and ROM as the source of truth; no JS-side interpretation of instructions.
- Register the example in the current multi-file WebRTL project selector, preserve current counter/CPU-bus/video/audio examples, and document how to compile, step/run/reset, inspect results, and reproduce failures.
- Measure/report browser compile time and simulation throughput for the example and any source-size, runtime, or feature limits that constrain this first CPU integration. Fix only limits necessary for this focused demonstration.

## Out of scope

- Full SNES console, PPU/APU, DMA, cartridge mappers, game ROM loading, or full commercial-game compatibility.
- Proving the entire 65C816 ISA, all timing quirks, interrupts, or cycle-perfect SNES bus behavior in this milestone.
- Arbitrary CPU debuggers, wide signal explorers, persistent project storage, FPGA place-and-route, or a general hardware plugin framework.
- Manual listening/device confirmation or other human-only merge gates.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The example contains a **genuine RTL 65C816 CPU implementation** connected to ROM/RAM; its source and license are documented and suitable for redistribution in this project.
- [ ] The provided multi-file example compiles and runs as **newly generated WASM entirely in the browser**, served under the static `/webrtl/` path without a compilation backend.
- [ ] The ROM contains verifiable machine-code instructions and a reset vector. Automated tests demonstrate instruction execution and expected PC/register or bus observations, including a RAM write/readback and deterministic PASS.
- [ ] Changing one test instruction, branch condition, or ROM data changes the observed RTL CPU behavior (or causes the documented FAIL); the browser is not running a prerecorded trace or interpreting the ROM in JavaScript.
- [ ] Reset restarts the CPU, memory, and test program deterministically; Step/Run/Pause behave coherently, including after recompile or failure.
- [ ] Existing browser examples still pass appropriate regression tests.
- [ ] HDL compatibility, reset and bus adaptation, memory map, test instructions/bytes, expected traces, and measured compilation/simulation performance are documented.
- [ ] The solution remains a small example/integration rather than an unrelated broad CPU or SNES framework; all required validation is automated or reproducible before merge.

## Optional validation

- Compare the test's instruction/register trace with an independent 65C816 software reference emulator.
- Try a second small CPU program and profile simulation bottlenecks.

## Required post-merge verification

After deployment, run an automated browser check against the GitHub Pages site that compiles the 65C816 example, executes the test ROM to PASS, and resets/repeats successfully. Report the actual result separately; publication is not a pre-merge gate.

## Related

- #3 — WebRTL project vision
- #12 — Multi-file browser projects (completed)
- #14 — CPU bus and ROM/RAM test harness (completed)
- #10 — Reusable video/audio outputs (completed)

Follow-up: connect CPU I/O, memory mapping, PPU/APU and controllers for a larger SNES hardware demo.
